retraction.reason: Re-read on 24 September under A14(6) against the rule that replaced M44b's. A record earns its place by carrying at least one honest edge to anything already in the atlas, and nobody writes an edge in order to keep a record. The corpus is now 859 active events across all five lanes, where M44b judged this one against the Portuguese core alone. Africa is in the atlas now, with 139 active events. The rising's own article, at revision 1370627418, opens its § Causes with "After the Scramble for Africa among the major European powers in the 1880s, Germany reinforced its hold on several formal African colonies." That sentence names the scramble rather than this rising, which is the chronology class this fire dropped nine A13 edges for. scramble-for-africa is an umbrella, a record other records are filed under, and batch 31a's rule keeps an umbrella off both ends of an edge. What this record wants is a place under that umbrella, since 1905 to 1907 falls inside 1885 to 1914. That is a filing and not an edge, so this pass cannot reinstate the record on it.

title: Majimaji War
summary: Wikidata item Q705553, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "Colonial war in the south and east of German East Africa, 1905-1907.". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
regionNote: The Wikidata import wrote this lane from the event's own point. The event points at no place record, so the timeline has nothing else to go on.
